author: Traditionally Moses
authorNote: Jewish and Christian tradition names Moses. Many modern scholars think the five books of the Law were drawn together from several sources over centuries, reaching their final form around the 6th–5th century BC; others defend substantial Mosaic authorship.
date: Traditionally c. 1400s BC; many scholars date its final form to c. 500s BC
overview: Genesis begins with God creating the world and humanity, and then tells how sin broke that good beginning. It follows the flood, the scattering of nations at Babel, and then narrows to one family: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph. God promises Abraham that through his descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed.
storyPlace: The very beginning. It sets up the problem (a broken world) and the promise (blessing through Abraham's family) that the rest of the Bible follows.
